walkthroughs.body_html: Scrooge's question 'Are there no prisons? Are there no workhouses?' directly echoes the 1834 Poor Law Amendment Act. Dickens shows that this law dehumanises the poor. The Present Ghost throws Scrooge's malthusian phrase 'surplus population' back at him, exposing its cruelty.

Scrooge keeps a 'very small fire' while Bob has even less. Fezziwig and the Cratchits, by contrast, blaze with light and laughter. Dickens makes warmth a moral currency: generosity literally heats the room. Scrooge's redemption is signalled when he orders the prize turkey and stokes Bob's fire.

Stave 1 describes Scrooge as 'solitary as an oyster' and cold as flint. Stave 5 calls him 'light as a feather, happy as an angel'. The complete reversal makes him an allegorical proof that even the hardest-hearted reader can change - Dickens hopes his Victorian audience will follow suit.
